rows.line: **(8)** The SIDE syllogism: all properties trace to the specification (Determination). If an off-line zero existed, some mechanism would produce it. The catalogue is exhaustive (Step 6). No single mechanism produces the coincidence (Step 7). No combination of mechanisms produces it either, because the inter-class couplings (product formula and distributive law) are spectrally inert — they carry no s-dependent information (Conservation). Contradiction. *This inter-class conservation step is the argument's one named premise: certified by Chapter 13 (the s-darkness of the product formula, from Tate's thesis), localized at a single compiled goal state, and stated in five equivalent registers (§27.3) — with everything surrounding it machine-checked.*

rows.line: The conclusion does not depend on the count 7. Whether the specification is parsed into 7, 8, or 10 classes, each class still identifies σ = 1/2 and none produces offline zeros. What matters is Ostrowski's guarantee that no place of ℚ is missed (exhaustiveness) and the per-class exclusion. Eleven major research programmes in analytic number theory — including the Selberg trace formula, random matrix theory, and the Langlands programme — decompose into combinations of C₁–C₇ with no eighth class.
